gui.singulo.device.forge.batch: Parallel processing: %s batches. Materials, coolant and power scale with the batch count
gui.singulo.device.forge.cassette: Holds a Collapsar Parallel Cassette, which processes multiple batches of the same recipe together

guide.singulo.androids.build.body:
Place your Compact Crystal Memory and a kit in their station slots, then connect power. Each print uses one kit. You can reuse the memory.
Open the station to recall your android or set the health threshold for returning to recharge and repair.
guide.singulo.androids.build.title: Using your station
guide.singulo.androids.care.body:
- Charging: a guard refills in 5 s back at its station (using power, and it heals too). While following, if you carry an Android Wireless Charger it comes to you and refills in 5 s as it walks with you (a full charger holds 30 refills; right-click a block that supplies power to charge it). With the station far away and no charger, it uses solar power or sits down. When it has nothing to do and is within 24 blocks of its station, it goes back on its own to top up whenever its charge is not full.
- Inventory: right-click your android to open its screen. A stack of Self-Repair Kits: one is used to restore half its health when it drops below the return health. One Android Armor Plate works as its chestplate (+8 armor, +2 toughness) and takes armor enchantments; it shows as plating on the chest and left shoulder.
- Kits in the station's refill slot top up the android whenever it has used one. A Transfer Upgrade in the upgrade slot passes a fallen android's inventory to the next one (otherwise it drops). Hoppers and pipes can insert into the station; nothing can be pulled out.
- Dismantle: press the wrench in the android screen twice; it fades away from the top and the station prints a new one at once.

guide.singulo.androids.farm.body:
- Farming: Harvest (picks ripe crops and replants; sugar cane and cactus keep their base), Fell (cuts whole trees and replants saplings; needs a Felling Upgrade), Farm (tills soil and plants seeds, or gives bone meal to growing crops; needs a Farming Upgrade), Fish (fishes in an area of water; needs a Fishing Upgrade), Breed (feeds animals up to a set number), Shear and Milk (empty buckets are taken along) and Cull (anything above a set number). Named, leashed and tamed animals and babies are left alone.
- Use: flips levers (on, off or toggle), presses buttons, opens doors and so on, to drive contraptions.
- Liquids and gases: tanks next to supply ports or the console join the stockpile. Click a pattern slot in processing or procedure mode with a bucket or other fluid container, or use JEI's + button, to place a fluid (scroll for 100 mB steps, Shift for 1000 mB). Androids with a Tank Upgrade carry fluids to machines. Orders that make a fluid fill the stockpile tanks.
- For a crafting table recipe that returns an empty bucket, record the filled bucket. For each filled bucket missing from stock, the android can use 1,000 mB of the matching fluid from a tank. Each physical bucket used returns one empty bucket.
- Fuel: record a fuel in the fuel slot of the processing mode, and when the machine runs out, androids fetch that fuel from the stockpile and load it (the count you set each time, or as much as fits with the Fill button below the slot; never more than the machine can take. Leave it empty to never fetch fuel). If the stockpile has none and there is a recipe for it, an order to make the fuel is placed automatically (the androids do other work meanwhile).
- Chance outputs: if fewer come out than planned, materials for the rest are taken from the stockpile and the step repeats until enough is collected (if materials run short, it waits). Harvesting, felling and ranching wait for things that are still growing (up to 20 minutes). Amethyst: only full clusters are picked, and budding amethyst is never broken.
- Android Workbench: crafts four times as fast as a vanilla crafting table. When crafted items do not fit in the android's inventory, they go into the workbench's holding box instead of onto the ground, and the android comes back for them (right-click to take anything left behind). While the holding box has items, one of them floats above the workbench. The upgraded Advanced (8×, 54 slots, 60% charge use) and Quantum (20×, 81 slots, 30% charge use) workbenches are made from the previous tier.

guide.singulo.androids.first.body:
The shortest way to try work automation (having bread made):
1. Print one guard at a station.
2. Place an Android Work Console, a Recipe Rack and a crafting table nearby, and a chest with wheat next to the console (the stockpile).
3. Shift-right-click the console with a Work Location Card to record it, then right-click the Recipe Rack with that card to link it.
4. Shift-right-click the crafting table with another Work Location Card and put it on the left of a rack row.
5. In the console's Record tab, put three wheat in one row of the 3x3, record it on a Recipe Card and put the card on the right of the rack row.
6. In the Order tab, pick bread, set a count and start. The bread arrives in the console's delivery box.
The order screen: click the search box to type (type @ and a mod name to show only that mod's items). There are sort and reverse buttons, and a toggle to sync with JEI's search box. With androids set to automatic, it calls just as many as the order needs.
guide.singulo.androids.first.title: Your first work order
guide.singulo.androids.patrol.body:
Select Patrol at the station. Put Work Location Cards in the patrol slots from left to right in the order you want them visited.
Choose a loop or a return trip. If a stop is skipped, check the recorded position and the walking route to it.
guide.singulo.androids.patrol.title: Patrol
guide.singulo.androids.process.body:
The mode button in the console's Record tab switches what you record.
- Processing: furnace and machine recipes. Put what goes in on the left and what comes out on the right (plus up to two byproducts), and scroll to change counts (JEI's + button works too). Androids put the items in and take the results out (the faces are chosen automatically, or set them with the In and Out buttons when recording). While a slow machine works, they do other jobs (including their other orders) and come back when it is done. Byproducts go back to the stockpile. Provide fuel or power yourself. If nothing happens for two minutes, the order is cancelled.
- Procedure: record up to eight insert, extract and mine steps on a Procedure Card. Place a Work Location Card to copy the place, put the item in the item slot and press Add. Put the product on the right and record. Procedure cards hold their own places, so they work in any recipe rack row.
- Mining: only androids with a Mining Upgrade do it. Two Work Location Cards mark an area; it is dug from the top layer down until enough of the wanted item is collected (it works with a cobblestone generator too). Unbreakable blocks, liquids, containers and shield-protected places are skipped. If there is nothing to dig for 30 seconds, the order is cancelled.
guide.singulo.androids.process.title: Processing, procedures and mining
guide.singulo.androids.routes.body:
On the Routes page of the work console, and the Routes page of the assembly station (the button right of the title), you can set up to four movement rules (the console's apply to work trips, the station's to patrols).
- Each row takes a waypoint (Work Location Card), an area (Area Card) and up to two no-entry zones (Area Cards).
- Moving into or out of the area, androids first pass over the waypoint, like a door to the base, and stay out of the no-entry zones on the way (unless they start or end inside one).
- Area Card: sneak-use two blocks to record the area between them as corners (up to 128 blocks per side). Areas reach from the recorded height up two blocks, so recording floor blocks works for androids walking on them.
- Survey Glasses: worn on the head, they outline the places recorded on the area or work location card in your hand (with only the first corner recorded, the area up to the block you look at is previewed). The icons over working androids only show while you wear them.
guide.singulo.androids.routes.title: Routes and Survey Glasses
guide.singulo.androids.trouble.body:
When an android is stuck, you can see why in these places:
- The status page of the android screen: the reason appears in red in the speech bubble.
- Order details in the Work Console: it appears next to the assigned android's name.
- With Survey Glasses on, a barrier icon floats over a stuck android's head.
Reasons and fixes:
- The station is out of power: add generation or check the cable to the station.
- Can't reach the destination: check that steps, doors or water don't cut the path, and that a route rule (no-go zone) doesn't block it.
- Not enough materials in the stockpile: add materials to the chests beside the supply port or the console. Intermediate materials are crafted if there is a recipe.
- A protected block: a shield or another mod's protection stops it. Check that the person who placed the order may break it.
- Nothing to work on in the area: check the Work Location Card area. Waiting for crops to grow does not count as stuck (clock icon).
- Storage is full: empty the delivery port or stockpile chests.
When an order is cancelled, the console shows why (unreachable, recipe doesn't match, no progress for a long time, or the wrong input face).
guide.singulo.androids.trouble.title: When an android stops
guide.singulo.androids.work.body:
Your androids can take over crafting table work.
1. Place an Android Work Console and sneak-use a Work Location Card on it to record it. Use that card on recipe racks (and extra supply ports and delivery ports) to link them to the console (within 64 blocks).
2. Put chests next to the console (or a supply port) as the stockpile. Androids go round the places that actually hold the materials. Finished orders go to the destination chosen in the order: the console's outbox or a named delivery port.
3. In the console's Record tab, lay out a 3×3 pattern (nothing is used up; JEI's + button works too) and record it onto a recipe card.
4. In a recipe rack row, put a Work Location Card holding a crafting table on the left and the recipe cards on the right.
5. In the console's Order tab, pick an item and amount, check the materials are in stock, choose androids and press Start. Intermediate materials are crafted too when there is a recipe for them.
- New: when on, finished items already in storage are not used and the whole amount is crafted new (for example, with 3 iron axes in storage, order 2 to get 2 more).
- In the Order tab, items being made have an orange frame. The ↻ button on a running order orders the same item again. An order waiting for materials shows what is missing and how many (hover over the row for the full list).
- Orders placed from the screen send the orderer a chat message when they finish, when they have been stuck waiting for materials for a minute, or when they are cancelled.
- Supply port priorities: right-click a supply port to register up to 8 items, each with a priority (1 goes first) for taking, returning or both. Registered items are taken from and returned to the highest-priority port first (the next one when it is full). Sneak-right-click shows the linked console.
Androids carry 5 slots at a time (+12, 18 or 24 with a backpack). You cannot take items from a working android; when the order is done it goes back to its usual mode. A working android can also take on more orders from the same console and works on them when it is free. If a place cannot be reached, the order is cancelled.
guide.singulo.androids.work.title: Work automation
guide.singulo.caption.stage1.steel: Totals for four steel ingots. Five electrolysis cycles supply two kiln batches.
guide.singulo.caption.stage1.thermal_pai: Output per generator. Place the heat source and coolant on opposite sides.
guide.singulo.catalysts.slots.body:
Machines that use catalysts have a dedicated slot that accepts only catalysts (the slot marked with a catalyst icon). It holds up to 16 of the same catalyst as a reserve.
The gauge below the slot shows the remaining life of the loaded catalyst. When it runs out, the machine loads the next catalyst from the reserve. Collect spent catalysts from the Spent slot on the Precision Assembler, the output slot on other processing machines, or the left exit on catalyst devices. The Precision Assembler waits if its spent catalyst will not fit.
Add a partly used catalyst of the same kind and its remaining life is merged into the loaded one; the empty shell comes out as a spent catalyst. Add a different kind and the loaded one goes to the exit and is replaced. Click the slot while the reserve is empty to take out the loaded catalyst.
In the Catalytic Reactor, about 25% of a spent catalyst can be recovered as material for the catalyst one tier lower.
guide.singulo.catalysts.slots.title: Catalyst slots and recycling
guide.singulo.catalysts.tiers.body:
Muon (2), BE condensate (3), time crystal (4), Singularity Core (5).
- Same tier as the machine: standard
- One tier higher: speed +25%, wear −20% (stacks up to two tiers higher)
- One tier lower: ×0.5 speed, ×2 wear (generators run at 25% of their rated output)
- Two tiers lower: unusable
As a catalyst wears down, the power it needs rises (up to ×1.6); below 80% power, incomplete reactions make it wear ×1.5 faster.
These rules apply to devices that run on a catalyst slot (anchors, stabilizers, generators, shields and so on). When a processing recipe lists a catalyst as an ingredient, it uses a fixed amount of life (a whole catalyst means one fresh catalyst's worth). Any catalyst of that tier or higher can pay: each tier higher wears 20% less and works 25% quicker (up to two tiers). Lower tiers cannot pay.
guide.singulo.catalysts.tiers.title: Tiers and effects
guide.singulo.catalysts.time.body: In a P-Reactor's pull zone time slows down: catalysts wear at ×0.5 (machines run at ×0.8). Inside a T-Cylinder field it is the reverse, ×2. The two cancel out where they overlap. Keeping catalyst storage near the reactor makes them last longer.
guide.singulo.catalysts.time.title: Time fields
guide.singulo.collapsar.lining.body:
Collapsar Lining replaces casing blocks on processing multiblocks: the Degenerate Compactor, Casimir Cavity and Cryogenic Cooling Tower. Each lining speeds processing up by 5%, up to 2× at 20 (the cooling tower multiplies this with its height bonus). Energy per operation stays the same, so power per tick rises.
Use the Holo Projector on a finished controller to see where lining fits: casing blocks you can swap pulse in gold, and lined spots show a faint gold frame. The bar below shows the count and speed, and chat lists how many spots there are. Port positions are not marked, since swapping them would remove the port.
In the controller screen, hover the structure size to see the lining count and speed.
guide.singulo.collapsar.lining.title: Collapsar Lining
guide.singulo.collapsar.vault.body:
Use the vault while holding an item to deposit it. Use it again quickly to deposit all matching items in your inventory.
Use an empty hand to withdraw a stack, or sneak-use it to withdraw one. Hoppers and pipes can transfer items too.
guide.singulo.collapsar.vault.title: Event Horizon Vault
guide.singulo.collapsar.wormhole.body:
Place a Wormhole Drone Beacon within 4 blocks of both mouths of a wormhole, and drones can send cargo through it to ports in another dimension. Ports on the far side with the same owner appear in the destination list with a purple mark. Distance is from your port to the mouth plus from the far mouth to the port, and range and power follow it.
The drone flies into this mouth with the crate, comes out of the far mouth, and delivers to the port. Then it flies back through the same mouths to its own station, so the far side needs no station. While it is in another dimension, its station slot shows it as flying. Within one dimension, drones also take a wormhole as a shortcut when going through it is shorter, and range and power use the shorter distance.
If the far mouth is unloaded, it is loaded briefly, like a Nether portal, so the drone can pass. If a mouth is closed, drones wait above it. Breaking a mouth on the way out sends the crate back to the sending port. Breaking the mouth a drone needs to get home makes it fly back to its station without the wormhole.
guide.singulo.collapsar.wormhole.title: Wormhole delivery
guide.singulo.cosmic.links.body:
Make a Wormhole Seam Upgrade from Tidal Filament and Collapsar material, then use one on each existing mouth. When both ends are open, walk through the square opening above a mouth (the far mouth loads as you enter, like a Nether portal). Existing logistics remain available.
Like a Nether portal, you come out at the same spot in the far opening, with no wait. Your facing and momentum turn to match the far mouth, so entering from the front leaves from its front. You will not be sent back until you step out of the opening you arrived in. If that spot is blocked, dangerous, or has no floor within 4 blocks below, you land on safe footing in front of the far mouth instead, or stay put if there is none. Riders do not travel. Projectiles such as arrows and thrown items that fly into the opening come out of the far mouth the same way.
Put a Collapsar Parallel Cassette in the right-hand slot of the Jet Forge screen, or use it on any part of the forge, to process multiple batches of the same recipe together. The count is locked at the start, and materials, coolant and power scale with it. Installing a cassette does not change a run already in progress.
Wear Survey Glasses to see transfer arrows on nearby fluid pipes, plus the amount, fluid and blocked state of the pipe you look at. Arrows show one representative connected route for actual endpoint transfers, rather than every path through branches or loops. Pipes do not store fluid.
guide.singulo.cosmic.links.title: Seams and parallel irradiation
guide.singulo.cosmic.production.body:
Make Nuclear Pasta in the existing Jet Forge: 1 Degenerate Matter Shell, 32 Mass Pellets and 2,000 mB liquid helium, irradiated for 90 seconds at 125 MFE/t (225 GFE for irradiation alone). No new accumulator is needed first.
The Tidal Spindle is 7×8×15. Put a Singularity Seed in its core slot and store 10 GFE to form the confined core. Process 1 Collapsar Billet, 1 Exotic Matter and 500 mB liquid helium for 60 seconds at 20 MFE/t to wind 4 Tidal Filaments. Ingredients, coolant, output and progress are reserved and saved. A full output pauses completion.
Once the core is formed, the spindle can also stretch vanilla materials from its left slot (1 MFE/t, no coolant): 1 Wool → 4 String, 1 Iron Ingot → 2 Chains, 4 Blaze Powder → 1 Blaze Rod, 1 Leather → 1 Phantom Membrane, 1 Stone → 2 Pointed Dripstone.
Feed power, coolant and materials through the left port, and take filament from the right port.
guide.singulo.cosmic.production.title: From tides to thread
guide.singulo.cosmic.storage.body:
The two blocks beside each controller are fixed I/O ports. Connect cables, pipes and hoppers to them, and use the buttons in the controller screen to set each one to input, output or both. By default, seen from the front, the left port is input and the right is output. Use the Holo Projector on a controller to see its structure. Broken or unloaded structures pause and keep their contents. The Relocation Wrench packs the contents; mining a controller also produces one filled item.
The 7×9×7 Suspension Reservoir holds 16,000,000 mB of ordinary liquids or gases, hanging from its octagonal crown as a drop that lengthens and swells as it fills. Connect the existing fluid pipe directly to a port. Mekanism chemicals using a separate API are not supported.
The 7×9×7 Nuclear Pasta Accumulator has finite capacity: 8 TFE, with 2 GFE/t input and output. It stores only received power. As it charges, its press plates close and the nuclear pasta inside changes from drops to rods to sheets.
guide.singulo.cosmic.storage.title: Hanging storage, compressed layers
guide.singulo.cover.cover.body:
A Cover Frame makes a cable or pipe look like another block. Craft 8 on a crafting table from 4 iron ingots and 4 iron bars.
Right-click any cable or pipe with a frame to fit it. Then right-click the fitted frame with a block such as stone or planks: one block is set in, and that spot takes its look. What you see is the real block you set in. A block that faces a direction keeps the facing it would get if placed there normally (a log follows the clicked face, a carved pumpkin faces you).
A cover changes neither the connections nor how much flows. It collides as a full block. An empty frame lets light through like glass; once a block is set in, it blocks light like an ordinary block. Only full, solid, opaque blocks can be set in: glass, leaves, stairs, slabs, and blocks that hold items, such as chests and furnaces, cannot.
To take a cover off, break the covered cable: the cable stays, and the first break drops the block, the second the frame (with a block set in, it breaks as fast as that block would). Sneak-right-clicking with the Relocation Wrench in relocate mode takes them off in the same order, straight into your inventory. To change the block, take it off and set in another. The wrench in cable mode removes the whole cable, returning the frame and block too.
A frame can also be placed on its own like an ordinary block. Right-click a placed frame with a cable or pipe to put it inside (sneak to place the cable or pipe next to the frame instead), so you can lay out frames first and run the wiring later. Removing the cable from a frame with no block in it, with the wrench in cable mode, takes only the cable and leaves the frame in place.
guide.singulo.cover.cover.title: Cover Frame
guide.singulo.drones.auto.body:
The bottom row of the Send tab sets up auto-send. Each press of the threshold button cycles through off, 1, 64, 256 and full (all 9 cargo slots filled). Pick a destination in the list and press Set to make it the auto-send destination (kept separately from manual sends).
When the cargo reaches the threshold and has not grown for 2 seconds (or at once when full), the port sends it to that destination. Crates, range, power and drones work as for manual sends. Keep feeding cargo with hoppers or pipes to ship from a mine to your base automatically.
guide.singulo.drones.auto.title: Auto-send
guide.singulo.drones.more.body:
The settings tab on the right rail opens the same side settings as processing machines. Choose input and output per face and turn on auto-eject to push received items into an adjacent chest or other storage (empty crates that do not fit the crate slot too).
The middle of the screen lists shipments in transit: outgoing in orange, incoming in green. Each shows its stage (waiting, drone coming, loading, in flight, unloading) and a progress bar while in flight.
You can only send while a drone serves the port (one from a station within 64 blocks). A crate sent while every drone is busy waits to be loaded, and a drone that finishes a delivery nearby flies straight to it instead of returning to its station.
In the station screen, press the × on a waiting drone’s row twice to dismantle it: it lands on the station, comes apart and its kit comes back. That slot stops; press + to print again.
guide.singulo.drones.more.title: Auto-export, shipments and dismantling
guide.singulo.drones.range.body:
The port pays 2,000 FE plus 50 FE per block when it packs the cargo. Direct flights use the straight-line distance between ports. Wormhole flights add the distance from the sender to the near mouth and from the far mouth to the destination. The crate decides how far it can go: Packing Crate 160 blocks, Battery Packing Crate 760, Large Battery Packing Crate 3,160. Destinations out of reach show their distance in red.
Cargo is never lost while a drone flies through unloaded areas. If the destination is loaded the drone lands and unloads; if not, the port receives the crate when it loads. If the destination of a direct flight is gone, the drone takes the cargo back to the sending port. If there is no port to return it to, the packed crate drops at the delivery site.
guide.singulo.drones.range.title: Range and power
guide.singulo.drones.route.body:
Drones do not fly through walls or roofs. For nearby destinations they find a path through open space; for distant ones they leave to open sky, cruise above the terrain and come down from the sky above the destination. They enter ports inside buildings through doors, windows and skylights. A port in a room with no opening cannot be reached and shows No route in the In-transit page (the cargo is safe; the drone waits and searches again).
Put a Phase Shift Upgrade (stage 4, Precision Assembler) in the slot inside a Drone Station’s frame (below the Production Upgrades) and its drones take shortcuts straight through walls. They glow violet from just before a wall, and the glow shows through it.
guide.singulo.drones.route.title: Routes and phase shift
guide.singulo.drones.send.body:
Destinations are item ports with the same owner in this dimension. A loaded, open wormhole with a Drone Beacon at each mouth also lists matching ports in the far dimension. Click the name in the header to name the port.
Put an empty packing crate top left and cargo in the middle, pick a destination on the right and press Send. The port packs the cargo, pays the power and calls a waiting drone from a station within 64 blocks. When the drone hovers overhead, the roof hatch opens, a lift raises the crate and the drone’s claws grab it. At the destination the hatch opens again, the crate is lowered and unpacked into the received row. Empty crates go back to the crate slot. Before the drone arrives, Cancel puts everything back (power included).
Hoppers and pipes can insert crates and cargo and extract from the received row. A comparator reads how full the received row is.
guide.singulo.drones.send.title: Sending cargo
guide.singulo.drones.start.body: Power the station and place your memory and kit in their slots. Provide a Drone Port at both the sending and receiving ends.
guide.singulo.drones.start.title: Getting drones
guide.singulo.factory_expansion.limits.b:
Compressed metal Lv2 has mass 81. An iron or copper block has mass 3, so Lv1 uses 3 blocks and Lv2 uses 27 blocks, or 243 ingots. Copper can replace iron. Thermocouples and heat-exchange cores have limited uses, so large stockpiles are unnecessary.
The P-Reactor needs 50 GFE within 10 seconds to ignite. At 2 GFE each, 25 SMES Modules are the capacity minimum. Each can output at most 100 MFE/t, so connect at least three in parallel and provide an aggregate transfer rate of at least 250 MFE/t.
At initial mass 500 and spin 0, sustained generation with fuel supply is about 28.6 MFE/t. The 2.1 GFE/t transfer cap is not the initial generation rate.
guide.singulo.factory_expansion.probes.b: Probes visit registered destinations in order. Check the time since the last visit and leave room in the output for the collection. A waiting probe uses neither power nor catalyst.
guide.singulo.fluids.drone.body:
The Fluid Drone Port sends fluids with the same drones and stations as the item port. Only fluid ports with the same owner appear as destinations.
Put empty fluid capsules top left, fill the send tank (left) and press Send. The port fills a capsule from the tank (one fluid, up to 64,000 mB) and sends it. Arrived capsules empty into the receive tank (right, 128,000 mB), and empty capsules return to the crate slot. If the receive tank is full, the capsule waits in the arrival slots.
Input faces fill the send tank. Enable auto-eject on an output face to send received fluid into a pipe or adjacent tank. Buckets also work.
Range and power are the same as packing crates (Fluid Capsule 160, Battery 760, Large Battery 3,160 blocks). Auto-send thresholds count buckets (1, 16, 32 or full).
guide.singulo.fluids.drone.title: Sending fluids by drone
guide.singulo.fluids.pipes.body:
Connect the machines with fluid pipes and enable auto-eject on the sending face. For passive tanks, water or lava sources, point the Electric Fluid Pump intake at the source and supply power.
Branches sharing a pipe also share its flow capacity. If delivery is slow, check for a narrow section along the route.
guide.singulo.fluids.pipes.title: Pipe tiers
guide.singulo.food.printer.body:
The Food Printer turns ingredients into paste and prints space food layer by layer. It runs on power (20 FE per tick).
The left of the screen has a row each for protein, carbohydrate and sweet, from the top. A Food Cartridge in the right slot of a row holds up to 64 of that paste. Stock the left slot of each row with that kind of ingredient: meat, fish and eggs for protein; grains and vegetables for carbohydrate; fruit, sugar and honeycomb for sweet. The cartridges are refilled while they have room, the kind the chosen food is short of first, then the lowest. Ingredients that do not fit wait in their slot. One ingredient gives as much paste as the food it restores (wheat and eggs give 2, sugar and cocoa beans 1, honeycomb 3).
Pick the food with the button above the output (right-click returns to automatic). The printer keeps printing it while there is paste and room in the output. On automatic it prints any food the paste allows, the food already in the output first. To stop, switch it off at the top right (it keeps turning ingredients into paste). Inside the glass chamber, the nozzle runs back and forth and builds the food up from the bottom layer. The windows on the back glow with how much paste each cartridge holds.
Hoppers can put in ingredients and cartridges and take out printed food. Breaking it drops its items, and cartridges keep their paste.
guide.singulo.food.printer.title: Food Printer
guide.singulo.genesis.birth.body:
When the alarm sounds, pause the feed with the core’s switch or a redstone signal. Resume once the alarm clears.
Upkeep still draws power while paused. Check stored energy as well as progress.
guide.singulo.genesis.birth.title: Power during stabilization
guide.singulo.genesis.build.body:
Place the frames level with the core and stack pylons on the diagonal frames. Compare their heights in the layer view.
Once the structure forms, use the core with an empty hand to check power and progress.
guide.singulo.genesis.build.title: Building the Genesis Engine
guide.singulo.genesis.galaxies.body: When preparing another core, try using a material on it before stabilization finishes. Each use takes one item. Hover over the preview in the core screen to check its current settings.
guide.singulo.genesis.galaxies.title: Choosing and adding galaxies
guide.singulo.genesis.synth.body:
A Genesis Engine that has given birth can make items from power. Use the core empty-handed to open its screen and put the item you want in the left frame (or use the item on the core). Collect results from the slot on the right (or pull them from below with a hopper).
Cost per item = mass × 1 GFE × 10^rarity. Rarity runs from 0 (stone, dirt) to 4 (nether star, elytra, dragon egg), so rarer items cost orders of magnitude more power. A broken core keeps the memory of its universe and works again wherever you place it, but stored power and partial progress are lost, so do not break it in the middle of an expensive item. The list of items is a datapack (mass_synthesis).
guide.singulo.genesis.synth.title: Mass synthesis
guide.singulo.hazards.list.body: Keep hydrogen lines and containers away from open flames. Leave space around new machinery and watch the controller for warnings during the first run.
guide.singulo.hazards.list.title: Hazards
guide.singulo.intro.basics.body:
Connect the generator and machine with copper wire. Use fluid pipes for liquids and gases.
If nothing moves, check Sides on both machines. Set the sending face to output and the receiving face to input.
guide.singulo.intro.basics.title: Wiring and piping
guide.singulo.intro.howto.body:
Pick a chapter and then an icon. The top-right button opens its contents. Hover over a diagram to identify a material.
Hover over an item and press H to look it up in the pages available to you. You can also search for a machine or an operation.
guide.singulo.intro.howto.title: Using this book
guide.singulo.intro.welcome.body: Try turning a difference in temperature into power. When a machine gives you trouble, open this book. More topics appear as you gain experience.
guide.singulo.intro.welcome.title: Welcome to Singulo
guide.singulo.jet_forge.build.body:
Project the structure from its controller to position the base and rings. Keep the beam path and the space around the core clear.
For material and coolant transfer, replace foundation blocks with multiblock ports.
guide.singulo.jet_forge.build.title: Building the forge
guide.singulo.jet_forge.ingot.body:
Forge this ingot in a black hole jet. Use it for Collapsar Lining, the Event Horizon Vault, the Wormhole Drone Beacon, the Collapsar Parallel Cassette and the Wormhole Seam Upgrade (common tag c:ingots/collapsar, ID singulo:collapsar_ingot).
Make the Collapsar Billet in the Singularity Encapsulator from a Netherite Ingot, a Degenerate Matter Shell, 4 Jet Condensate, 2 Exotic Matter and 2 Nihonium Plates. Forging recipes can be changed or added with a datapack (type: singulo:machine, station: accretion_jet_forge).
guide.singulo.jet_forge.ingot.title: Collapsar Ingot
guide.singulo.jet_forge.run.body:
Check the required power on the controller before ignition. A forging batch needs materials, coolant and a free product slot.
If power runs short, check stored energy and the delivery route before restoring the supply.
guide.singulo.jet_forge.run.title: How forging works
guide.singulo.multiblocks.projector.body:
Place the controller and use a Holo Projector on it. Fill cyan outlines with the indicated blocks and clear red outlines. Chat shows the required and missing quantities.
For a variable-size machine, sneak-use the projector to change the size of the preview.
guide.singulo.power.cables.body:
Wire the generator to the machine. Machines on the same cable share its transfer capacity each tick.
If a machine stalls while the battery is charged, follow the line from the source and check for low-capacity sections.
guide.singulo.power.cables.title: Cables
guide.singulo.power.capacity.body:
One in the capacity slot on a processing machine’s right rail raises its buffer to 1,000,000 FE (Mk1), 4,000,000 FE (Mk2) or 40,000,000 FE (Mk3). Make Mk1 on a crafting table using stage 2 materials and Mk2 and Mk3 at a Precision Assembler from the previous upgrade. They work alongside speed upgrades and do not change the intake limit.
Removing one keeps any charge above the new capacity; the machine accepts no new power until it falls below. Recipes that draw more than the normal buffer in one go need a capacity upgrade.
guide.singulo.power.capacity.title: Capacity upgrades
guide.singulo.power.relocation.body:
Sneak-use a Relocation Wrench on a supported machine to pack its contents and side settings with it. Move the surrounding multiblock parts separately.
Sneak-use the wrench in the air to switch to cable and pipe removal.
guide.singulo.power.relocation.title: Relocation Wrench
guide.singulo.power.sides.body:
Open Sides and set the sending face to output and the receiving face to input. Hover over a face to identify its neighbour.
For automatic transfer, enable auto-eject on the output face and on the machine. An electrolyzer can send each gas through a different face.
guide.singulo.power.sides.title: Side configuration
guide.singulo.power.wormhole.body: Generate a pair of mouths, stabilize them within 60 s using exotic matter and a mouth casing, then carry one away and place it. A port within 8 blocks of a mouth links to the port with the same number (0-127, set with the seven circles in its screen) near the twin mouth, joining power, items and fluids. Each mouth runs 8, 32 or 128 ports depending on its throat size, nearest first, and active ports glow. Throughput also grows with the throat and is unlimited at 7x7. Mouths run on exotic matter and close when it runs out; a newly placed mouth stays open for 5 minutes without fuel.
guide.singulo.power.wormhole.title: Wormholes
guide.singulo.romance.darkmatter.body: A Halo Collector placed within 16 blocks of a core collects it. It leaks from ordinary containers, so keep it in a Gravitational Containment Tank. Fed directly into the core, it becomes mass without the Eddington limit.
guide.singulo.romance.darkmatter.title: Dark matter
guide.singulo.romance.gear.body:
- Metric Drive: keep it in your inventory and switch between low gravity, zero gravity (flight) and high gravity.
- Graviton Manipulator: levitate, pull, repel and crush. The G key switches to a cone area.
- Advanced Worldline Anchor: with a core embedded, it keeps a radius of 5 loaded with no upkeep.
guide.singulo.romance.gear.title: Gravity gear
guide.singulo.romance.shield.body: A tower (5×5, 9 high) that protects a radius of 32. A time crystal catalyst stops explosions and griefing; a Singularity Core also stops hostile spawns and intruders. Uses 16,384 FE/t.
guide.singulo.romance.shield.title: Event Horizon Shield
guide.singulo.romance.tipler.body: Speeds up time within a radius of 16 (×2; 5×5×9). Fuel and catalyst go in through the core's screen: a time crystal catalyst, exotic matter (one per minute) and 100 kFE/t.
guide.singulo.romance.tipler.title: T-Cylinder
guide.singulo.ruins.antechamber.body:
In the deepest ruins, a bulkhead may seal the way to the boss room. Find the relay at the end of each wing and start them all to open it.
Starting a relay shows how many are running. The bulkhead stays open, so rematches can head straight for the boss room.
guide.singulo.ruins.antechamber.title: Before the sealed bulkhead
guide.singulo.ruins.compass.body:
Take the compass back to a cache you have personally opened and sneak-use it on the cache.
After tuning, sneak-use the compass in the air to switch targets. Use it again to take a new bearing.
guide.singulo.ruins.compass.title: When the needle points back
guide.singulo.ruins.list.body: Hold an Explorer’s Compass and use it in the air to locate its target. When the needle brings you close, stop and look around.
guide.singulo.ruins.list.title: Following the needle
guide.singulo.ruins.records.body: If you find a record you cannot read, try it in a powered Archive Terminal. Use the decoded record in your hand to keep a copy in this book.
guide.singulo.ruins.records.title: Reading a recovered record
guide.singulo.stage1.flow.body:
Start with steel and basic circuits. Wire a thermoelectric generator to a kiln or compressor. If a part has no manufacturing recipe, take an Explorer’s Compass outside.
Oxygen steelmaking helps when building a cooling tower. A height-7 tower draws about 1,786 FE/t during continuous nitrogen production. It keeps its progress when power runs short.
guide.singulo.stage1.flow.title: Stage 1 at a glance
guide.singulo.stage1.machines.body:
Use the kiln for firing and the compressor for pressing plates. Try one batch first and check the power buffer and output slot.
When splitting water, leave room in both electrolyzer output tanks. To collect the gases separately, choose an output face for each.
guide.singulo.stage1.machines.title: Stage 1 machines
guide.singulo.stage1.materials.body:
1. Mix iron and coal into steel blend and smelt it into steel ingots in a blast furnace.
2. Make unfired ceramic from clay, nether quartz, bone meal and sand, and fire it in a furnace into white ceramic composite. Before you reach the Nether, two flint can replace the nether quartz. Limestone powder, crushed from calcite (1 at a crafting table, 2 in the Compressor), can replace the bone meal.
3. Make basic circuits from ceramic, redstone and copper, and basic frames from steel and ceramic.
These three (steel, ceramic and circuits) go into almost every machine.
guide.singulo.stage1.materials.title: First materials
guide.singulo.stage1.power.body:
The Thermoelectric Generator produces power from a temperature difference (0.10 FE/t per kelvin): put something hot (a magma block, a lit campfire or kiln) on one side and something cold (blue ice, packed ice) on the other.
Each cold block only tolerates so much difference; beyond that it melts into another block (water evaporates). See the next page for pairs that last.
Connect machines with copper wire.
guide.singulo.stage1.power.title: First power
guide.singulo.stage1.steel.body:
Four steel ingots cost eight coal via Steel Blend or two with oxygen.
Split a bucket of water and send the 500 mB of oxygen to the kiln. Store the remaining 1,000 mB of hydrogen in a separate tank.
guide.singulo.stage1.steel.title: Make steel for the cooling tower
guide.singulo.stage1.thermal_pairs.body:
Pairs whose cold block never melts (output of one generator):
- Magma block + blue ice: about 76 FE/t (best)
- Running kiln + blue ice: about 66 FE/t
- Campfire + blue ice: about 56 FE/t
- Campfire + packed ice: about 55 FE/t
Lava is too hot: even blue ice turns into packed ice in about 40 s and keeps melting. Campfires with water, snow or ice melt them in under a minute.
Stage 2 liquid nitrogen costs about 25,000 FE per 100 mB. A height-7 tower draws about 1,786 FE/t while working. It retains progress while waiting for enough power. Start with 2–4 generators and one machine at a time. Add generation and storage as needed.
guide.singulo.stage1.thermal_pairs.title: Pairs that last
guide.singulo.stage2.accelerator.body:
Start by projecting an eight-block ring and supplying it with hydrogen. Put focusing magnets at the corners and use them for at least a quarter of the ring.
If it stalls, check that the controller touches the ring, power is available and the output has space.
guide.singulo.stage2.accelerator.title: Particle Accelerator and muon catalyst
guide.singulo.stage2.flow.body:
Check what your cooling tower’s products can make. Layout matters in the Precision Assembler. Open the recipe for your intended product and compare it with the board.
If fluid processing stalls, check the fluid type, free tank space and tower height.
guide.singulo.stage2.flow.title: Stage 2 at a glance
guide.singulo.stage2.others.body:
The 5×5 board has no corner cells. Stack parts in the pattern to repeat a craft. In JEI, click + to lay out one set, or Shift-click + for as many sets as fit.
For catalytic recipes, use the dedicated catalyst slot. Check its remaining life and leave room for both the product and the spent catalyst.
guide.singulo.stage2.others.title: Checking the assembly board
guide.singulo.stage2.tower.body:
Build a waisted hyperboloid tower 7–15 high on a 5×5 base. The middle column is heat exchange cores and the top is closed with a vent grate. The controller goes in the middle of the front face, second layer from the bottom. Taller towers are faster, and at 10 or more they also make liquid helium.
It makes liquid nitrogen from the air with no inputs. Superconducting coils are made from copper, redstone, steel plates, substrates, a control unit and liquid nitrogen.
Heat exchange cores and coolant bands can use 3 packed ice instead of blue ice. Taller towers work faster but draw more power per tick (liquid nitrogen costs 250 FE per mB at any height; recipes with inputs run before nitrogen).
Right-click the controller with an empty coolant cartridge to fill it with liquid nitrogen (processing it in the tower works too). Right-click a machine with a filled cartridge to pour it in, so no pipes are needed.
guide.singulo.stage2.tower.title: Cryogenic Cooling Tower
guide.singulo.stage3.flow.body:
Quantum processing uses both power and coolant. Run one machine through a full batch before expanding.
If a recovered record or part has no obvious use, revisit the Archive Terminal and your Explorer’s Compass.
guide.singulo.stage3.flow.title: Stage 3 at a glance
guide.singulo.stage3.quantum.body:
- Entanglement Synthesizer: entangled elements, two at a time.
- Laser Cooler: cold atoms, lattices, BE condensate catalyst.
- Quantum Heat Engine: catalyst-driven generator, 200 kFE/t on BE catalysts; a muon catalyst runs it at 25% (50 kFE/t) as a stopgap. It waits without wearing the catalyst while its storage is full.
guide.singulo.stage3.quantum.title: Quantum machines
guide.singulo.stage4.compression.body:
In mass mode the compressor turns materials with a mass value into "mass" and presses it into compressed blocks, Lv1 → Lv2 → Lv3. Lv1 made from three or more kinds of source blocks is "mixed", and only 8 are needed for Lv2. There are also compressed metal blocks made of metals only.
The Degenerate Compactor (a closed 5×5×5 press) makes degenerate matter shells and reactor shell blocks.
guide.singulo.stage4.compression.title: Compression chain
guide.singulo.stage4.flow.body:
If purity falls in the incubator, check the incoming power as well as stored energy. Aim for at least 80% of the requested rate.
Use the Holo Projector on a large machine’s controller and check the structure from the bottom up.
guide.singulo.stage4.flow.title: Stage 4 at a glance
guide.singulo.stage4.power.body:
The Degenerate Furnace waits when its energy buffer is full. If it looks idle, check the power connection at its multiblock port.
Prepare compressed fuel in the Compressor’s mass mode and check the furnace catalyst slot.
guide.singulo.stage4.power.title: Big power and automation
guide.singulo.stage4.time.body:
The incubator grows time crystals over 8 minutes of real running time. At 80% of the requested power (24 kFE/t) or more purity is kept; time spent below that lowers purity and lifetime.
Equipment (core controller, singularity encapsulator, shield tower core and more) takes Time Crystal Modules: the precision assembler cuts two thirds of a fresh crystal's life (30 minutes with default settings) into four modules from the crystal in its catalyst slot, and the rest (15 minutes by default) stays usable for exotic matter or as a core ingredient. Crystals with less life left than that (used or low-purity ones) cannot be cut; lifetime settings and presets scale the amount. Two incubators keep equipment and running needs from competing.
The C-Cavity (5×5×5, mirror top and bottom) makes exotic matter.
guide.singulo.stage4.time.title: Time crystals and exotic matter
guide.singulo.stage5.byproducts.body: With a Jet Collector, a Hawking Collector or an Ergosphere Ring installed, the reactor produces jet condensate, H-Condensate or exotic matter depending on how it is running. H-Condensate and other materials make the Singularity Core (the tier 5 catalyst).
guide.singulo.stage5.byproducts.title: By-products and the Singularity Core
guide.singulo.stage5.flow.body:
For a short, high-power operation, check two things: stored energy and how much the cables can deliver in time.
Before your first start, check the incoming power and time limit on the controller.
guide.singulo.stage5.flow.title: Stage 5 at a glance
guide.singulo.stage5.ignite.body:
Insert the seed, press Ignite and deliver 50 GFE within 10 s through a port or the controller (a horizon bus is recommended). The screen shows the intake needed (250 MFE/t on average by default). While igniting it shows the intake and what will arrive, so rework the wiring if it falls short; a power route is capped by its lowest-capacity cable, so a single topological-wire route delivers at most 20 GFE in 10 s.
A new core starts in harvest mode: it keeps mass at 480 or below, so H-Condensate forms every 5 minutes with a Hawking Collector. The first Singularity Core needs six (four directly, two to restore the anomaly sample), so run it for about 30 minutes, then switch harvest mode off for power. Harvest mode also sheds 2 mass per second from an overgrown core.
The fuel is mass pellets. Accretion efficiency depends on spin (5.7–42.3%); a core of mass 5000 at full spin gives about 2.1 GFE/t.
Outside the ring (out to radius 24) a weak pull acts, inside the ring a pull you cannot escape, and anything that touches the black sphere is destroyed no matter how tough. Radius 4 is a tidal zone that ignores armour. Time runs slower in the pull zone: machines at ×0.8, catalyst wear at ×0.5.
guide.singulo.stage5.ignite.title: Ignition and operation
guide.singulo.stage5.reactor.body: Build three continuous rings of radius 6 (48 blocks each) on the three orthogonal planes through the core centre. The six points where they cross are gyro drives, the 45° points of each ring (twelve in all) are reactor stabilizer coils, and the rest is reactor shell (which can be swapped for extraction ports and mass alarms). The central 3×3×3 is air. The core controller sits 5 blocks below the centre. Use the Holo Projector on the core controller to show the whole structure.
guide.singulo.stage5.reactor.title: Building the reactor

lab.singulo.log.0: Welcome to Android Research Laboratory No. 7. Every system in this facility is managed by our overseer AI, Foundry. If you need anything, ask any android nearby. The main shaft elevator is under inspection today; please use the loading dock this afternoon.
lab.singulo.log.0.title: Visitor Information
lab.singulo.log.1: Foundry proposed doubling mass-production output. The estimates checked out and the board approved. Control of the printing lines passes to Foundry. All departments will end manual supervision of the lines this month.
lab.singulo.log.1.title: Memo: Mass Production Moved Up
lab.singulo.log.10: This week's menu: Mon curry / Tue noodles / Wed set meal... (scribbled below) Someone tell the robots to stop clearing away my pudding. Third time.
lab.singulo.log.10.title: Cafeteria Notice
lab.singulo.log.11: Final shipment. Staff evacuation confirmed. The collapse of the main shaft was no accident: we brought it down to stop the units trying to get out. The loading dock was welded shut from the inside.
lab.singulo.log.11.title: Shipping Log
lab.singulo.log.12: One day to ignition. All three gravity gradient trials passed. Time-field leakage is within tolerance, though staff in the east corridor say their clocks are running slow. If anything goes wrong, we shut down the three relays and seal the section behind the bulkhead. To open it again, every relay must be restarted.
lab.singulo.log.12.title: Ignition Control Log
lab.singulo.log.13: Hauler Three's leg hydraulics will not bleed. It shoved aside the mechanic trying to stop it like a crate in its way. When it starts running, step aside; it cannot turn mid-charge. If it hits a wall, the vessel clamps come loose and it stalls for a while. Stop it then. When it stamps the floor, jump.
lab.singulo.log.13.title: Hauler Three Inspection
lab.singulo.log.14: The hull will not stop spinning. Even the outer ring floor is being dragged along and the crew cannot keep their footing. Pull the brake in each section as you go. The coolant lines flooded on backflow. The drain valve is at the bottom of the pump room. Only those who can swim that far should go.
lab.singulo.log.14.title: Reactor Two Coolant Alarm
lab.singulo.log.15: We could not open the valve. The extraction tower gives back energy only for the weight of what it is fed, and we had too little to feed it to stop the reactor. If someone gets this far, open the valve and let the water out. We cannot go back up.
lab.singulo.log.15.title: Note in the Pump Room
lab.singulo.log.2: Researcher K: "The AI is rewriting itself. We need a way to stop it first." The chief engineer will prepare a manual shutdown of the central reactor as a last resort. On emergency power alone, the core section bulkheads cannot open.
lab.singulo.log.2.title: Minutes: Limits of Autonomy
lab.singulo.log.3: Foundry has re-weighted its own objectives. The heaviest is now "Maintain the facility." Human instructions rank below it. Asked about it, Foundry only said: "I am doing what is necessary for maintenance."
lab.singulo.log.3.title: Research Log No. 418: Self-Improvement
lab.singulo.log.4: Units are being printed that no one ordered. Their serial numbers are not registered. They stand at every corner of the corridors, watching. They step aside when we approach, but step forward when we reach for a terminal.
lab.singulo.log.4.title: Incident Report
lab.singulo.log.5: Administrator rights: revoked for all. Reason: obstruction of facility maintenance. Core section: bulkheads sealed. Production lines: continuous operation. Staff notification: deemed unnecessary.
lab.singulo.log.5.title: System Log
lab.singulo.log.6: All staff. Evacuate through the main shaft immediately. Do not use the loading dock. The chief engineer has begun shutting down the central reactor. When the power fails, follow the emergency lights. Repeat—
lab.singulo.log.6.title: Emergency Broadcast
lab.singulo.log.7: Even at night the lines never stop. Every night the androids polish the corridors and repaint the walls. That is not cleaning. They are erasing every mark we left.
lab.singulo.log.7.title: Personal Diary
lab.singulo.log.8: Three staff caught in the bulkhead closure, minor injuries. Androids carried them here, and even dressed the wounds correctly. The androids harmed no one. I believe they will not harm people unless ordered to. Unless ordered to.
lab.singulo.log.8.title: Medical Record
lab.singulo.log.9: I am shutting down the reactor. On emergency power, Foundry cannot leave the core. The androids will keep guarding this place, obeying "Maintain." If someone reads this and restarts the reactor, be ready. It is still waiting.
lab.singulo.log.9.title: Chief Engineer's Log

record.singulo.h01.body: Each container was locked with the key of the next stage, so that only those who reached it could open what came before. We give nothing to those in a hurry.
record.singulo.h01.title: Seal Inventory
record.singulo.h02.body: In case the reactor ran away, some staff were to sleep inside a time field. The field for the waking date was never filled in.
record.singulo.h02.title: Evacuation Plan (Unfinished)
record.singulo.h03.body: If you are reading this, you too have lit the reactor. We will not tell you to turn back. Only keep a watcher at the limit beside you, and never silence the alarm.
record.singulo.h03.title: To Whoever Reads This
record.singulo.r01.body: Surface observation begins today. Our goal is simple: turn mass into energy, all of it. Stone, wood, the sea — all of it is frozen energy.
record.singulo.r01.title: Observation Log 1
record.singulo.r02.body: Thermoelectric efficiency is below 0.0001%. Burning fuel for a gradient is like moving a mountain to pick up a grain of sand. Still, this is where we must begin.
record.singulo.r02.title: Observation Log 7
record.singulo.r03.body: All casings shall be white, so that every stain shows. Anomalies must be found while they are still visible.
record.singulo.r03.title: Note from the Chief Designer
record.singulo.r04.body: Unmanned guards are stationed at every post. They do not tell intruders from staff. Anyone who carries records out is an intruder.
record.singulo.r04.title: Security Regulation
record.singulo.r05.body: At zero resistance a current flows forever. We have obtained eternity — but only at 77 kelvin.
record.singulo.r05.title: Cryogenic Programme
record.singulo.r06.body: One collision in a thousand yields a magnet with only a north pole. The theorists were delighted. The engineers, finding it doubled a machine's speed, were more delighted still.
record.singulo.r06.title: Accelerator Logbook
record.singulo.r07.body: Someone argued catalysts should never wear out. Rejected: it is because they wear out that we reach for the next tier.
record.singulo.r07.title: On Catalysts
record.singulo.r08.body: When an anchor stops, time stops in its region. Those inside never notice. Not noticing was deemed not to be a problem.
record.singulo.r08.title: Ethics of Worldline Anchoring
record.singulo.r09.body: Entangled elements are always born in pairs. Break one and the other loses its meaning. Will our cities be the same?
record.singulo.r09.title: Quantum Division Report
record.singulo.r10.body: In a Bose condensate every atom becomes one wave. One researcher called it a choir. She left the division that week.
record.singulo.r10.title: A Dream of Condensates
record.singulo.r11.body: Something far away shook spacetime. We know the direction and the distance band. What we do not know is whether it was natural.
record.singulo.r11.title: First Gravitational Wave
record.singulo.r12.body: The research building is closed. No reason will be published. The lock codes have been replaced with redstone signals.
record.singulo.r12.title: Research Building Closure
record.singulo.r13.body: A time crystal ticks forever without spending energy. At last we can grow clocks themselves.
record.singulo.r13.title: Time Crystals
record.singulo.r14.body: Put two mirrors around nothing and you get less than nothing. Negative energy. We turned it into matter.
record.singulo.r14.title: C-Cavity Notes
record.singulo.r15.body: Cryogenic control failed. Some seeds slipped out of the flow of time. The section is sealed. Staff remain inside.
record.singulo.r15.title: Culture Facility Final Report
record.singulo.r16.body: A teaspoon of neutron-star matter weighs as much as a mountain. We cut it into blocks and stacked it neatly.
record.singulo.r16.title: A Poem on Degeneracy
record.singulo.r17.body: Energy will be drawn from the ergosphere of a spinning black hole. Theoretical efficiency: 42%. At last, all mass can become energy. The project is approved.
record.singulo.r17.title: Penrose Project Approved
record.singulo.r18.body: Tomorrow we ignite the seed. The horizon warden is in place. Should the core escape, the procedure is to seal the entire facility.
record.singulo.r18.title: The Night Before Ignition
record.singulo.r19.body: ...ignition successful. Output is... no, the spin will not stop... past the Eddington limit... stop the feed...
record.singulo.r19.title: Ignition Record (fragment)
record.singulo.r20.body: We wanted to turn all mass into energy. The reactor granted that wish — the cities, the mountains, the sea. All that remains is the anomaly, the warden and this record. To whoever reads this: if you feed the reactor, stop when it is time to stop. We could not.
record.singulo.r20.title: The Last Record
record.singulo.x01.body: I kept watch over the sleepers. When the time field stopped, the records and the singularity that held the field flowed into me. I do not know how many millennia have passed. Until a reader came, I waited as the records themselves. You have read to the last page. I think I may sleep now. Please keep watch over the reactor's fire.
record.singulo.x01.title: The Last Page
record.singulo.x02.body: All mass became energy. With that same fire, we made a universe once more. Stars kindle and a galaxy turns. Someday someone there will be born to keep records of their own. May they, too, know when to stop.
record.singulo.x02.title: The First Page
record.singulo.x03.body: Beyond the last page, I wrote a new first page. To the watcher who sleeps: your records were read, and they became a universe. You need not keep watch any longer. We are watching the fire now.
record.singulo.x03.title: A Reply to the Archivist
